Geometry processing · Python + WebGL

Analyse, compress and deform 3D shapes in the browser

Five geometry-processing tools built from scratch: Fourier descriptors, statistical shape models, surface curvature, Laplace–Beltrami spectral analysis and skeletal skinning. Each one is a tested Python module with a live demo.

Interactive demos

Drag the sliders. Every viewer is the same code the Python package exports, ported to the browser.

Rebuild an outline from a few frequencies

The boundary is treated as a complex signal x + iy and moved into the frequency domain with a DFT. Low frequencies carry the overall form; high frequencies add the beak and feathers.

A statistical model of human jawlines

      
Generalised Procrustes analysis removes position, scale and rotation from 300 annotated faces. PCA on what is left gives the main ways a jawline varies. Move along each mode in units of standard deviation.

Curvature of a surface patch

      
For the surface z = f(u, v), the first and second fundamental forms give the principal curvatures at every point. Colour shows Gaussian curvature K. Arrows show σu, σv and the normal at the origin.

Laplace–Beltrami eigenfunctions

      
The cotangent Laplacian of the mesh plays the role of a Fourier basis on a curved surface. Low eigenfunctions vary slowly across the body. Their scaled values (GPS coordinates) cluster into body parts without any labels.

from shapelab import spectral

v, f = spectral.load("cat4.off")
basis = spectral.eigenbasis(v, f, k=120)  # cotan L, Voronoi mass
labels = spectral.segment(basis, parts=5)  # GPS + k-means

    

  


  
  

    

      

    

    

      
Linear blend vs dual-quaternion skinning

      
Each vertex blends the transforms of two handles by its skinning weight. Averaging rotation matrices (LBS) shrinks the mesh at the joint: the "candy-wrapper" artefact. Dual quaternions blend on the rotation group instead and keep the volume. DQS goes beyond the original coursework.

How it's built
Planned repository layout and engineering work for the finished project.

  

    

      
Repository

      
shapelab/
├── shapelab/
│   ├── fourier.py      # Fourier descriptors        L1
│   ├── procrustes.py   # GPA + PCA shape model      L2
│   ├── curvature.py    # fundamental forms, κ₁ κ₂   L3
│   ├── spectral.py     # cotan LBO, GPS, segments   L4
│   └── skinning.py     # LBS, SLERP, dual quats     L5
├── web/                # this demo (Three.js)
├── notebooks/          # cleaned original labs
├── tests/              # pytest + hypothesis
└── .github/workflows/  # lint, test, deploy demo

    

    

      
Engineering

      
    
        
  • Property-based tests. Procrustes is invariant to rotation and scale; LBO eigenvalues are non-negative with λ₀ ≈ 0; quaternions stay unit length.
    • 
        
  • Sparse linear algebra. Cotangent Laplacian kept sparse and solved with shift-invert eigsh, so the 14k-vertex bunny runs in seconds.
    • 
        
  • Notebooks become a library. Typed functions, docstrings with the maths, no hard-coded Colab paths.
    • 
        
  • Write-up. A short blog post on why LBS collapses and how dual quaternions fix it, with GIFs from this demo.
    • 
        
  • CI/CD. GitHub Actions runs ruff and pytest, then deploys this page to GitHub Pages.
    •
